papers.title: Preregistered Test of Quantum Resonance Theory's Bell-State Fidelity Prediction on Superconducting Quantum Hardware
papers.authors: Amber Anson (sole contributor)
papers.venue_year: OSF Registries, OSF Preregistration schema, registered 3 July 2026, public
papers.identifier: https://osf.io/yg923 (OSF registration; a 10.17605/OSF.IO/... DOI is likely but I did NOT verify one)
papers.what_it_establishes: The only genuinely prospective, publicly time-stamped pre-registration of a quantum-hardware prediction that I could find anywhere. It states a point prediction from Quantum Resonance Theory (Anson 2024, Zenodo) that a weak stroboscopic phase drive (R0 = 1e-3 rad, 10 MHz, with 1/5/20/50 MHz off-resonance comparators) raises Bell-state fidelity by ~5%, against standard QM predicting no gain; fixes the design (IBM Quantum least-busy open-access backend, 30 circuits x 8000 shots = 240,000 shots, parity-based fidelity, bootstrap 95% CI with 4000 resamples); and fixes the decision rule in advance (H1 requires G >= +2.5% with CI excluding zero and the 10 MHz effect exceeding all off-resonance points; falsification if the CI upper bound < +2.5%). The registration explicitly states that data does not yet exist and that the only prior execution was a non-evidential simulator pipeline check.
papers.overlap_reason: Direct overlap on the methodological lens only: prediction committed publicly and datably before measurement, pre-specified falsification criterion, superconducting hardware, commitment to publish regardless of outcome. Scientifically disjoint from the material (fringe-theory drive test versus shadow/SWAP estimator calibration). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I could NOT verify that any outcome was ever reported. The OSF project page is a JavaScript app that did not render for me; the registration has zero child components; no arXiv paper reporting the result exists (arXiv search for 'Quantum Resonance Theory' in quant-ph returns two unrelated 2008/2017 papers). Two web-search summaries asserted the prediction 'was falsified as specified', but the OSF API description I did read is the PLAN and states data does not yet exist, so those summaries most likely paraphrased the conditional falsification rule. Treat the outcome as unverified.

papers.title: Understanding Side-Channel Vulnerabilities in Superconducting Qubit Readout Architectures
papers.authors: Satvik Maurya, Chaithanya Naik Mude, Benjamin Lienhard, Swamit Tannu
papers.venue_year: IEEE International Conference on Quantum Computing and Engineering (QCE), pp. 1177-1183, 2024
papers.what_it_establishes: Defines and measures exactly the material's crosstalk quantity: P_flip(A) = Pr(A_meas=1 | A_prep=0, V), i.e. the 0->1 readout error of a qubit conditioned on the full bitstring V of the other qubits sharing the feedline. Sweeps ALL 2^4 (and 2^5) neighbour bitstrings, so the excitation-weight axis is present in their raw data. Measured P_flip runs ~0.02-0.08 for most attacker placements and reaches ~0.3 for one configuration, against a baseline excitation rate shown as a dashed line. Data is a 5-qubit frequency-multiplexed transmon device (readout-trace dataset from Lienhard et al.), NOT a cloud vendor machine. Verified from full text: they present per-bitstring bar charts and feed them to an SVM state classifier; they never analyse how P_flip scales with the NUMBER of excited neighbours, and the words 'saturate', 'Hamming', and 'number of excited' do not appear.
papers.overlap_reason: Same measured quantity as the material's P(1|0)-vs-neighbour-excitation result, on the same physical mechanism (shared Purcell-filtered feedline), with comparable magnitudes. The material's saturation-with-weight claim is the one thing this paper's data could have shown but does not report. Must be cited; the paper should state explicitly what it adds beyond Maurya et al.

papers.title: I Know What You Are Reading: Evaluating Readout Crosstalk in Cloud-based Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Yizhuo Tan, Jakub Szefer
papers.venue_year: Proceedings of the 2025 Quantum Security and Privacy Workshop (QSec '25), Taipei, October 2025
papers.what_it_establishes: The closest platform match. Measures readout crosstalk on Rigetti Ankaa-3 accessed through a public cloud path (qBraid), using circuits containing only X gates and measurements. Protocol: hold a spectator qubit in |0>, set subsets of neighbouring target qubits to |0> or |1>, and record how often the spectator reads 1. Their worked example: spectator measured 1 in 40/1000 shots with targets in |0> versus 310/1000 with targets in |1> -- i.e. 4% -> 31%, the same order as the material's 1.6% -> 16.9%. Six subset patterns x 2 measurement sets per spectator, over spectators 8, 9, 15, 16; a Random Forest Regressor attributes the effect to individual target qubits and reconstructs the likely shared-feedline map. Verified from full text: they also state they could not find Rigetti documentation showing which qubits share readout feed lines.
papers.overlap_reason: Same vendor lineage (Rigetti, prior generation), same cloud-access framing, same conditional-readout-error measurement, same magnitude class. This is the paper a referee will reach for first. It also pre-empts a weaker version of the 'vendor does not publish it' theme, though only for feedline topology, not readout error rates. They vary how many targets are excited but analyse it as feature attribution, never as a weight-dependence curve.

papers.title: Categorizing Readout Error Correlations on Near Term Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Benjamin Nachman, Michael R. Geller
papers.what_it_establishes: THE CLOSEST PRIOR ART TO THE MATERIAL'S CROSSTALK RESULT, and it is not currently cited. Defines exactly the quantity the material measures. Their 'A-type correlator' is A_ij = <E_1^i>_{|0...0>} - <E_1^i>_{X_j|0...0>}: the change in qubit i's readout error when spectator qubit j is excited by an X gate. That is, term for term, the material's 'P(1|0) on one qubit rises from 1.6% with idle neighbours to 16.9% with excited ones,' restricted to a single excited neighbour. They also define C-type measurement-operator covariances. Deployed on IBMQ Melbourne (15 qubits) and IBMQ Manhattan (65 qubits). FINDINGS THAT CUT AGAINST OUR MATERIAL BEING FIRST ON THE CONCEPT: correlations exist and are measurable. FINDINGS THAT CUT IN OUR FAVOUR ON MAGNITUDE AND STRUCTURE: they conclude the correlations are SMALL relative to single-qubit readout error (Melbourne typically below 1%, Manhattan reaching several percent against per-qubit errors of 1-10%), and they report the surprising geometry that on Melbourne 'there is nearly no correlation between the size of the A_ij and qubit-qubit distance,' while Manhattan's long-range correlations are 'consistent with statistical noise.' DECISIVE GAP: they excite spectators ONE AT A TIME. They do not vary the number or weight of excited spectators, and there is no analysis of accumulation versus saturation. They also make no claims about three-or-more-qubit correlations and do not study temporal dynamics.
papers.overlap_reason: DIRECT on the observable, and the material must cite it or a referee will. Any claim of the form 'we discovered that readout error depends on neighbouring excitations' is already established here for single spectators on IBM hardware. Three things survive as the material's own. (1) MAGNITUDE AND PLATFORM: Nachman and Geller's headline is that this effect is small compared to single-qubit readout error; the material reports a ~10x swing (1.6% -> 16.9%) that is LARGER than the single-qubit rate, on Rigetti rather than IBM, i.e. a quantitative reversal of their reassuring conclusion on different hardware. (2) THE WEIGHT LAW: saturation with excitation weight rather than accumulation is genuinely absent from this paper and, as far as I could find, from the literature (an arXiv abstract search for readout + crosstalk + Hamming weight returned zero results). The operational corollary the material draws, that the correction must therefore be measured at each weight rather than extrapolated from single-spectator data, is a direct and non-obvious critique of exactly this paper's measurement design. (3) CONSEQUENCE: they characterize; the material shows the effect propagating into a specific failed physical estimate and then closing it. Recommend citing as the definitional precedent while foregrounding the weight-resolved result as the delta.

papers.title: Efficient reconstruction, benchmarking and validation of cross-talk models in readout noise in near-term quantum devices
papers.authors: Jan Tuziemski, Filip B. Maciejewski, Joanna Majsak, Oskar Slowik, Marcin Kotowski, Katarzyna Kowalczyk-Murynka, Piotr Podziemski, Michal Oszmaniec
papers.venue_year: arXiv Nov 2023; Open Systems & Information Dynamics (World Scientific), 2025
papers.what_it_establishes: Quantum Detector Overlapping Tomography (QDOT), with sample complexity logarithmic in qubit number. Its 'correlated clusters and neighbours' model is Lambda_{x|y} = prod_chi Lambda^{y_N_chi}_{x_C_chi | y_C_chi}: the noise matrix acting on cluster C_chi depends explicitly on the pre-measurement state y_N_chi of its neighbourhood N_chi. Applied to 79-qubit Rigetti Aspen-M-3 and 127-qubit IBM Cusco; correlation coefficients plotted above a 3% threshold for IBM and a 7% threshold for Rigetti; ~20% improvement in model-based mitigation for MAX-2-SAT energy estimation. Verified from full text: the model conditions on the full neighbour BIT PATTERN, and the words 'saturat', 'Hamming', and 'excited' do not appear anywhere in the paper.
papers.overlap_reason: State-conditioned readout noise on a Rigetti device at scale -- the most general published formalism covering the material's effect. Weight-saturation is representable in their model but is never measured or discussed, which is what leaves the material's finding open. The 7% Rigetti correlation threshold is a useful magnitude anchor for the material's numbers.

papers.title: Amazon Braket launches Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q superconducting device (vendor documentation, not a paper)
papers.authors: AWS Quantum Technologies Blog
papers.what_it_establishes: Quotes 108 qubits across twelve 9-qubit chiplets in a 3x4 array and 99.1% median CZ fidelity, and states that Amazon Braket provides up-to-date calibration data for all qubits and qubit pairs on Cepheus-1-108Q, including single-qubit gate fidelities, two-qubit gate fidelities, AND readout errors, accessible via the console or the Braket Python SDK.
papers.overlap_reason: Not prior art but a direct factual hazard to the material's central framing. The claim 'readout error is absent from that specification' is falsifiable in one click for this exact device via a different access path. The claim must be narrowed to the Open Quantum / Quantum Rings Public Tier route actually used -- where per-job calibration metadata was unavailable -- and must distinguish per-qubit readout error (published by Braket) from CORRELATED, neighbour-conditioned readout error (published by no vendor I found).

papers.title: Raw-Curve Quantum Fingerprints: A Mahalanobis Authentication Framework with Drift Early Warning and Adversarial Detection
papers.authors: Geyuyan Ma, Xiangdong Meng, Yangyang Fei, Zhiqiang Fan, Hanshi Zhao, Chenhui Wang, Haoran Yang, Weilong Wang, Zheng Shan
papers.what_it_establishes: Opens with the exact premise of the material: 'Quantum cloud platforms are poised to deliver powerful computing capabilities, but users have no direct means to verify which physical device executes their workload. This lack of transparency enables hardware substitution attacks, where a malicious adversary could redirect a job to a substituted or inferior processor.' Builds device fingerprints from raw measurement statistics (no curve fitting), 100% benign authentication on three superconducting processors over a three-week chronological split, plus drift early-warning and adversarial-perturbation detection. Establishes that (a) the unverifiable-execution-path problem is a named, published problem, and (b) it is solvable well enough that fingerprinting works across weeks of drift.
papers.overlap_reason: Shares the material's core premise verbatim in spirit (user cannot confirm which device ran the job) and works over multi-week drift on superconducting hardware. Diverges completely in purpose: this is an adversarial security countermeasure paper that PROPOSES a fix, whereas the material REPORTS the unverifiability as an accepted methodological limitation of a physics measurement and does not attempt device authentication. Also does not address decentralized/mediated (non-vendor) routing. Does NOT preempt the pre-registration methodology or the specification-gap diagnosis.

papers.title: A Graph-Based Forensic Framework for Inferring Hardware Noise of Cloud Quantum Backend
papers.authors: Subrata Das, Archisman Ghosh, Swaroop Ghosh
papers.what_it_establishes: States that circuit execution 'depends on internal allocation and routing policies that are not observable to the user,' that 'users cannot verify whether their circuits were executed on the hardware for which they were charged,' and that a provider may redirect jobs to more error-prone regions 'while still presenting stale or averaged calibration data.' Uses a Graph Neural Network to reconstruct a per-qubit and per-link error map WITHOUT calibration data from the target backend, so users can compare inferred error rates against published specifications; reported mismatch ~22% single-qubit, ~18% link.
papers.overlap_reason: This is the closest published statement of two of the material's three framing problems at once: the unobservable execution path AND the gap between provider-published specification and actual device behaviour. Critically, it also anticipates the remedy of user-side inference when per-job calibration metadata is unavailable — exactly the situation the material reports. Does NOT overlap on: pre-registration, readout error specifically as the missing specification input, correlated readout saturating with excitation weight, cross-session purity drift, or the non-monotonicity.

papers.title: Works on My QPU: Reproducibility in Quantum Computing Research
papers.authors: Dominik Köster, Maja Franz, Benjamin Zec, Nicole Hoess, Ralf Ramsauer, Wolfgang Mauerer
papers.what_it_establishes: The current state-of-the-art reproducibility audit of the field: 127 papers manually assessed against a five-question framework (RQ1 code availability, RQ2 environment specification, RQ3 build/run documentation, RQ4 HARDWARE SPECIFICATION, RQ5 executability), plus automated screening of ~5,000 papers. Only 24.4% provide code; 64.5% of those fail to execute in a clean environment; ~1/3 lack machine-readable environment specs. On hardware specifically it establishes that among papers using real QPUs with code, only three specify the target hardware in sufficient detail; that hardware execution 'cannot be replicated by a reproduction package per se'; that 'access to quantum devices is often limited or changes over time'; and recommends shipping raw measurement data plus calibration snapshots so partial reproduction survives loss of the original device.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes the field-level reproducibility deficit the material's contribution would sit inside, and names calibration-snapshot provisioning and hardware specification as reproducibility requirements — directly relevant to the material's finding that per-job calibration metadata was unavailable. But it is a bibliometric meta-study of published artifacts, not a hardware measurement: it does not itself run circuits, does not quantify cross-session drift, and does not address mediated or decentralized execution paths. It gives the material a citation anchor and a normative framework, not competition.

papers.title: Claim against Measurement: Statistical Artefacts in Quantum Error Mitigation Benchmarks
papers.authors: Dominik Köster, Wolfgang Mauerer
papers.what_it_establishes: Systematic review of 81 QEM papers plus a 72-hour longitudinal hardware study on IQM Euro-Q-Exa (LRZ Garching), with secondary validation on ibm_brussels. Design: a fixed Trotter circuit (6 CZ) measured every 30 min, 147 time points, n_reps=30 per point, split into two 12-hour day sessions and one 48-hour weekend session. Reports variance attributable to time of measurement (eta^2) of 0.35 (day 1, 12 h), 0.20 (day 2, 12 h) and 0.55 (weekend, 48 h), with lag-1 autocorrelation 0.55 / 0.21 / 0.83 respectively; effective independent observations collapse from a nominal 30 to as few as 1.8. Concludes that the same ZNE configuration can show an effect size more than 3x larger purely depending on when it ran, and proposes longitudinal drift assessment as a minimum reporting standard.
papers.overlap: PARTIAL (DIRECT on the "drift dominates statistical error, and grows with the observation window" claim)
papers.overlap_reason: This is the single strongest competitor for the material's stability contribution. It already establishes, quantitatively and on superconducting hardware, that (a) reported statistical error bars understate real uncertainty because drift violates independence, and (b) variance attributable to time grows sharply when the window extends from 12 h to 48 h — structurally the same statement as "cross-session drift ~20x within-session drift". Differences that leave room: their observable is a ZNE-mitigated expectation value, not state purity; they report an eta^2 variance fraction per window rather than an explicit within-session vs cross-session ratio on byte-identical circuits pinned to the same physical qubits; no register-size non-monotonicity; and no pre-registration. Any claim of novelty for the drift result must cite and differentiate from this paper.

papers.title: Characterizing the Reproducibility of Noisy Quantum Circuits
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Travis S. Humble
papers.what_it_establishes: Directly assesses reproducibility of a noisy quantum circuit via Hellinger distance between computational results, and shows that DEVICE CHARACTERIZATION offers an analytic bound on the observed variability. Validated on an ensemble of single-qubit test circuits on a superconducting transmon processor 'with well-characterized readout and gate error rates.' Concludes that a composite device parameter defines an upper bound on observed Hellinger distance across circuits.
papers.overlap_reason: Load-bearing and possibly NOT yet cited — the material cites dasgupta2021stability and dasgupta2022assessing, and this Entropy 2022 paper is a distinct third work in the same programme. It matters because it argues the OPPOSITE polarity to the material: published device characterization is claimed to bound reproducibility. The material's central negative result is that the published characterization did NOT bound the outcome, precisely because the binding input (readout error) was absent from the specification. Note their validation explicitly assumed WELL-CHARACTERIZED readout error, which is the assumption the material breaks. This should be cited and contrasted, not merely listed.

papers.title: Routing Anonymity and Identifiability of Noisy Quantum Hardware
papers.authors: Ben Priestley, Mina Doosti
papers.what_it_establishes: Formalizes a 'backend-identifiability game' as a security notion for quantum cloud routing: providers may wish to hide implementation details, scheduling choices, or which physical device was used, but noisy finite-shot outputs carry backend-specific fingerprints in the classical output distribution. Experiments on Amazon Braket across Rigetti Ankaa-3 and IQM Garnet (superconducting) and IonQ Aria-1 (ion trap): 87–90% classification between superconducting backends, 96–100% across platforms. Identifiability survives natural post-processing.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes that hiding the execution path is a recognized provider behaviour with a formal name, and — importantly for the material — that shot-level outputs from RIGETTI superconducting hardware on an aggregator (Braket) carry enough signal to identify the backend. That means the material's 'execution path cannot be independently verified' is a statement about the ABSENCE OF AN ATTEMPT, not a proven impossibility; a referee may ask why the material did not fingerprint. Overlap is on the premise and platform only, not on pre-registration, purity, drift magnitude, or the specification gap.

papers.title: Detecting Fraudulent Services on Quantum Cloud Platforms via Dynamic Fingerprinting
papers.authors: Jindi Wu, Tianjie Hu, Qun Li
papers.what_it_establishes: Targets 'machine substitution' and 'profile fabrication' attacks — a cloud provider misrepresenting which quantum device executed user code, potentially swapping in a simulator or inferior hardware. Method uses a single dynamic probing circuit capturing device-specific error patterns; the user compares a device-side fingerprint against a user-side fingerprint generated by a linear-complexity algorithm. Validated on seven IBM Quantum devices.
papers.overlap_reason: Names 'profile fabrication' — a provider publishing a device profile that does not match the executing hardware — which is structurally the same failure the material encountered (published specification did not describe the device that ran the job), though the material attributes it to an incomplete spec rather than fraud. Earliest of the substitution-detection cluster, so it establishes the priority date for the problem statement. No overlap on methodology (pre-registration), on physical findings, or on decentralized routing.

papers.title: Entropy Density Benchmarking of Near-Term Quantum Circuits
papers.authors: Marine Demarty, James Mills, Kenza Hammam, Raul Garcia-Patron
papers.venue_year: arXiv preprint, submitted 23 Dec 2024, revised 15 Jan 2026
papers.what_it_establishes: Estimates purity and Renyi-2 entropy density of VQA circuit outputs as a function of circuit depth on Rigetti's Aspen-M-3 QPU using the Pauli version of classical shadows (K=1000 snapshots per setting, M=50 settings). Compares hardware purity/entropy against numerical simulation of the same circuits under a local depolarising noise model whose parameters were deduced from Aspen-M-3 calibration data. Builds heuristic entropy-accumulation models to bound circuit-size thresholds for quantum advantage.
papers.overlap_reason: This is the closest published analogue in my lens: purity estimation from randomized/shadow measurements on Rigetti superconducting hardware, with an explicit predicted-vs-measured comparison driven by a calibration-derived noise model. The material differs on four axes: (i) predictions were pre-registered to version control before submission rather than compared post hoc; (ii) the estimator is a two-copy destructive SWAP test, not single-copy Pauli shadows; (iii) the noise model here is local depolarising from vendor calibration, whereas the material's central result is that the calibration-derived model fails and the missing input is unpublished readout error plus correlated readout crosstalk; (iv) no cross-session drift analysis. Verified from the abstract page and corroborating search snippets of the methods; I did not read the full text.

papers.title: Quantum advantage in learning from experiments
papers.authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Michael Broughton, Jordan Cotler, Sitan Chen, Jerry Li, Masoud Mohseni, Hartmut Neven, Ryan Babbush, Richard Kueng, John Preskill, Jarrod R. McClean
papers.what_it_establishes: The canonical hardware demonstration that entangled two-copy (Bell-basis) measurements beat single-copy measurements exponentially in sample complexity for learning tasks including property prediction, quantum principal component analysis, and learning physical dynamics. Proof-of-principle experiments on up to 40 superconducting qubits and ~1300 gates on Google Sycamore, with the advantage surviving noisy quantum memory and processor.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes the single-copy vs collective (two-copy) hardware comparison that the material sits inside, on superconducting hardware, and is unavoidable prior art for any collective-measurement claim. But it is an advantage demonstration: it shows the separation survives noise, not that a two-copy purity prediction misses by 17 standard errors. It does not pre-register predictions, does not close an error budget against measured readout and crosstalk, and does not study cross-session reproducibility. Abstract verified; the 46-page supplement (which would contain any error budget) was not read.

papers.title: Approaching optimal entangling collective measurements on quantum computing platforms
papers.authors: Lorcan O. Conlon, Tobias Vogl, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Simon K. Yung, Falk Eilenberger, Dominic W. Berry, Fabiana S. Santana, Rainer Blatt, Thomas Monz, Ping Koy Lam, Syed M. Assad
papers.what_it_establishes: Experimentally implements theoretically optimal single-copy AND two-copy collective measurements for simultaneously estimating two non-commuting qubit rotations, across superconducting, trapped-ion and photonic platforms. Reports that the metrological gain from collective measurement persists under significant decoherence, and that error mitigation was needed to reach the Nagaoka bounds.
papers.overlap_reason: A direct hardware demonstration of two-copy collective measurement on superconducting devices, explicitly benchmarked single-copy vs two-copy, and it reports that raw hardware falls short of the theoretical bound until mitigation is applied - structurally the same shape as the material's 0.8932-predicted / 0.7184-measured gap. It differs in target quantity (non-commuting rotation estimation, not purity), it is not pre-registered, and it attributes the shortfall to generic decoherence rather than isolating an unpublished readout channel. Search snippets reported IBM Q System One, cloud IBM Q, and Rigetti Aspen-9 as the superconducting platforms; I verified title/authors/venue/abstract on arXiv but could NOT confirm the specific device list or the error budget from the abstract page.

papers.title: Transition from statistical to hardware-limited scaling in photonic quantum state reconstruction
papers.authors: Attila Baumann, Zsolt Kis, Janos Koltai, Gabor Vattay
papers.venue_year: Phys. Rev. A (2026), DOI 10.1103/3gsc-krrq; arXiv Mar 2026, rev Jun 2026
papers.what_it_establishes: Experimentally characterizes a hardware-induced systematic error floor in shadow tomography on integrated photonic processors. Reconstruction error initially follows the statistical O(M^-1/2) scaling, then abruptly saturates at a floor set by spectral distortions of the realized unitary ensemble - a sharp transition into a bias-dominated regime that cannot be beaten by collecting more samples. Decouples static coherent spectral distortion from dynamic decoherence.
papers.overlap_reason: This is the published precedent for the material's bias-floor concept: a randomized-measurement estimator on real hardware whose accuracy stops improving with shots because a systematic hardware bias dominates. It is the paper most likely to be raised against a novelty claim framed around 'budget-independent bias floor'. Distinctions: photonic integrated processor not superconducting; the floor is attributed to unitary-ensemble spectral distortion rather than to unpublished readout error and excitation-dependent readout crosstalk; no two-copy/SWAP estimator; no pre-registration; no cross-session analysis. Abstract verified only.

papers.title: Development and Demonstration of an Efficient Readout Error Mitigation Technique for use in NISQ Algorithms
papers.authors: Andrew Arrasmith, Andrew Patterson, Alice Boughton, Marco Paini
papers.what_it_establishes: Readout-error mitigation built on approximate state estimation and classical shadows, demonstrated on Rigetti hardware. Random measurements symmetrise readout error so mitigation needs O(1) calibration samples with qubit count; the abstract explicitly claims the approach can suppress the effect of CORRELATED readout errors. Reports collecting and processing 10^6 samples in under 1.5 minutes.
papers.overlap_reason: Directly prior on the material's central causal claim - that correlated readout error is the load-bearing term in a randomized-measurement error budget on Rigetti hardware - and it is by Rigetti-affiliated authors. However it MITIGATES correlated readout rather than characterizing its structure: I found no evidence it measures how P(1|0) scales with the number of excited neighbours, nor that the dependence saturates with excitation weight. It also does not do purity, two-copy measurement, pre-registration, or session variation. Abstract verified; the specific Rigetti device and measured readout rates were not obtainable from the abstract page.

papers.title: Demonstration of robust and efficient quantum property learning with shallow shadows
papers.authors: Hong-Ye Hu et al. (10 authors)
papers.what_it_establishes: Robust shallow-shadow protocol demonstrated on a superconducting quantum processor (search snippets indicate 18 qubits on a 127-qubit device), recovering expectation values, fidelity and entanglement entropy. Uses Bayesian inference to learn and mitigate an experimentally relevant noise model. States explicitly that noise accumulates with each added circuit layer and biases the estimate, and that mitigation trades bias for estimator variance; error-mitigated shadow predictions and fiducial measurements agree within their stated uncertainties.
papers.overlap_reason: A superconducting hardware demonstration of randomized-measurement property learning that names bias, bias-variance trade-off, and residual systematic error as the central experimental concerns - the same vocabulary as the material. But its headline is that after mitigation NO significant unmitigated systematic bias remains, which is close to the opposite of the material's finding of a persistent bias floor. No two-copy estimator, no purity-via-SWAP, no pre-registration, no cross-session drift. Abstract verified; qubit count came from a search snippet, not from the paper.

papers.title: Practical Tests and Witnesses of Fermionic non-Gaussianity
papers.authors: Tobias Haug, Xhek Turkeshi, Piotr Sierant
papers.what_it_establishes: Introduces fermionic antiflatness and two measurement protocols for it: a two-copy Bell measurement and a single-copy scheme using commuting Majorana bilinears. Run on the IQM quantum processor, finding that noise can both reduce and enhance the measured non-Gaussianity. Includes a purity-corrected witness for mixed states, claimed robust under strong noise.
papers.overlap_reason: A recent hardware paper that implements BOTH a two-copy collective protocol and a single-copy alternative for the same quantity, with purity correction - the same protocol dichotomy the material studies, on superconducting hardware, in 2026. Different target quantity (fermionic non-Gaussianity, not Bell-state purity), no pre-registration, and the abstract discloses no readout-error rates, crosstalk, drift, or session-variation data. Abstract verified only; I could not confirm whether both protocols were actually run on IQM or only one.

papers.title: Noisy Quantum Learning Theory
papers.authors: Jordan Cotler, Weiyuan Gong, Anand Kannan
papers.what_it_establishes: Theoretical framework (introduces a complexity class NBQP) for learning from noisy quantum systems. Key result for this lens: the exponential two-copy advantage for PURITY TESTING collapses under local depolarizing noise. Also treats Pauli shadow tomography under noise and Heisenberg-limited metrology. A setting motivated by AdS/CFT restores the advantage via noise-resilient structure.
papers.overlap_reason: This is the theoretical statement of the material's empirical result: the two-copy advantage for purity specifically does not survive realistic device noise. Any reviewer will ask how the material's hardware finding relates to this theorem. Crucial distinction to make explicit: this is pure theory under an idealized local depolarizing model, whereas the material's collapse is driven by an entirely different and non-depolarizing mechanism - unpublished readout error, excitation-correlated readout crosstalk, and cross-session drift - none of which this paper models. Abstract verified only.

papers.title: Stability of noisy quantum computing devices
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Travis S. Humble
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED WORK #1. Characterizes four device metrics via Hellinger distance across temporal and spatial scales: initialization fidelity F_I = 1 - e_R (i.e. one minus readout error), CNOT gate fidelity from randomized benchmarking, duty cycle tau = T2/T_gate, and 'addressability' F_A = 1 - normalized mutual information between register elements at measurement. DATA SOURCE IS SPLIT AND THIS MATTERS: the 22-month series (March 2019 - December 2020, 673 daily calibration records, 445 with gate duration) is IBM's OWN PUBLISHED CALIBRATION DATA for the 5-qubit ibmq_yorktown, not circuits the authors ran. Their own executions are confined to a SINGLE DAY on the 27-qubit ibmq_toronto (11 December 2020, six windows 08:00-23:30, 5,750,784 register observations), using fiducial separable and Bell states. Temporal stability H(t) = d_H(F_X(t-tau), F_X(t)) on sliding 1- and 3-month windows; spatial stability H(i,j) between register pairs. Addressability on toronto ranges 0.8875 (pair 23,21) to 0.9989 (pair 11,13). Verbatim from the abstract: 'Our observations collected over 22 months reveal large fluctuations in each metric that underscore the limited scales on which current NISQ devices may be considered reliable.' EXPLICIT NON-CLAIMS: no tolerance threshold is defined ('Whether this later behavior is sufficiently stable depends on the given application'); Bell-state addressability was 'limited to only nearest-neighbor register pairs'; the addressability metric is acknowledged to be state-dependent; no calibration cadence or acceptance criterion is proposed; no error-mitigation technique is evaluated.
papers.overlap_reason: Shares the thesis that superconducting device parameters fluctuate on scales that break reproducibility, and it does look at readout error and at pairwise measurement correlations. But the overlap stops at three boundaries the material crosses. (1) PROVENANCE OF THE NUMBERS: their long series is VENDOR-PUBLISHED calibration data; the material's central finding is that the vendor number is the one that is wrong and unpublished (~6.5% measured vs 2% assumed, ~3x), which by construction cannot be found in a study whose long-baseline input is the vendor's own record. (2) TIMESCALE STRUCTURE: their own-execution data is one day, so they cannot separate within-session from cross-session variation; the material's headline is that ratio (~1% per qubit within-session propagating to ~0.01 in purity, versus ~0.2 in purity across sessions on byte-identical circuits and the same physical qubits, roughly twenty times larger). (3) OBSERVABLE: they characterize device metrics, not an application-level derived quantity against a locked prediction. The material adds: an independently measured readout rate, a within-vs-cross-session ratio on identical circuits, and a pre-registered prediction that the fluctuation broke.

papers.title: Measuring NISQ Gate-Based Qubit Stability Using a 1+1 Field Theory and Cycle Benchmarking (journal version appears as "Measuring qubit stability in a gate-based NISQ hardware processor", Quantum Inf. Process., DOI 10.1007/s11128-023-03826-4 — I could NOT verify the arXiv/journal equivalence directly, Springer blocked fetch)
papers.authors: Kubra Yeter-Aydeniz, Zachary Parks, Aadithya Nair, Erik Gustafson, Alexander F. Kemper, Raphael C. Pooser, Yannick Meurice, Patrick Dreher
papers.venue_year: arXiv preprint, Jan 2022 (quant-ph); journal version Quantum Information Processing, 2023
papers.what_it_establishes: Runs a transverse-field Ising / 1+1 field-theory application repeatedly on ibmq_boeblingen (20-qubit superconducting transmon) at the same time each day on different days, and at different times within the same day. Verbatim from the body: "We observed both inter-day and intra-day calibration drifts on the ibmq_boeblingen processor"; results at different times "should have similar results that fall within each graph's error bars... Figure 5 and Figure 10 clearly show that this is not the case"; and "The processor is substantially drifting from day to day despite both the daily IBM RB re-calibrations and even intra-day (morning and night) IBM re-calibrations." Their Table 1 also shows qubit 6 readout error rising 2.54% -> 9.19% and T1 dropping 67.1 -> 24.1 us over five days.
papers.overlap: PARTIAL (DIRECT on the qualitative cross-session claim)
papers.overlap_reason: This is the closest superconducting-platform precedent for the claim that identical circuits on the same physical qubits do not reproduce within error bars across sessions, and it explicitly separates inter-day from intra-day drift. It does NOT give a numerical ratio between the two (no analogue of 0.2 vs 0.01 in purity), does not use a purity/SWAP-test or shadow observable, and is on IBM hardware with published per-job calibration. Their readout error excursion to 9.19% also means "measured readout far exceeds the assumed/spec value" is not itself a novel observation.

papers.title: Assessing the stability of noisy quantum computation
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Travis S. Humble
papers.venue_year: arXiv Aug 2022; SPIE Quantum Communications and Quantum Imaging XX proceedings, 2022
papers.what_it_establishes: Frames computational accuracy, result reproducibility, device reliability and program stability as distinct, operationally defined concepts, and derives bounds on program output stability in terms of device reliability.
papers.overlap_reason: Already cited in the material (dasgupta2022assessing). Supplies the vocabulary and the formal reliability-to-stability link that the material's drift section will inevitably be read against, but contains no measurement of a purity-like quantity across sessions.

papers.title: Impact of unreliable devices on stability of quantum computations
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Travis S. Humble
papers.what_it_establishes: Quantitatively bounds the reliability of circuit outcomes in terms of the Hellinger distance between noise distributions at different times, yielding thresholds on how frequently hardware must be recalibrated to guarantee statistical reproducibility. Validated with synthetic and experimental noise data from a superconducting device.
papers.overlap_reason: Gives a formal recalibration-interval criterion — i.e. it already answers "how far apart can two runs be before results stop being comparable", which is the theoretical shape of the material's 0.2 vs 0.01 finding. Overlap is with the interpretation, not with the specific measurement.

papers.title: Anchor: Reducing Temporal and Spatial Output Performance Variability on Quantum Computers
papers.authors: Yuqian Huo, Daniel Leeds, Jason Ludmir, Nicholas S. DiBrita, Tirthak Patel
papers.venue_year: Proceedings of ACM SIGMETRICS 2026; arXiv Oct 2025
papers.what_it_establishes: Documents that identical programs give inconsistent outputs across days and across machines, then mitigates it with a linear-programming qubit-mapping method. Simulation on five 27-qubit IBM machines (Cairo, Hanoi, Algiers, Mumbai, Kolkata); hardware validation on five 127-qubit IBM machines (Sherbrooke, Kyiv, Brisbane, Brussels, Strasbourg) over a two-day window, with training data collected over about a week specifically to cover temporally varying noise. Reports total-variation-distance standard deviations of 5.9% (Anchor) vs 8.8% (OptiMap) vs 17.8% (random mapping), and a 73% average reduction in variability; on IBM Hanoi over five days baseline TVD often exceeds 20% while Anchor stays around 12-15%.
papers.overlap_reason: Quantifies day-to-day output variability of byte-identical programs on superconducting hardware and reports its magnitude, which is the closest published numeric analogue to the material's cross-session purity spread. But it treats variability as a thing to engineer away rather than characterize; it uses TVD of bitstring distributions, not purity; it does not decompose within-session vs across-session; and it is a systems/mapping paper, not a physics characterization.

papers.title: A Preparation Nonstationarity Loophole in Superconducting-Qubit Bell Tests
papers.authors: Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, Ramakrishna Podila
papers.what_it_establishes: Shows that the standard assumption that repeated circuit executions sample a single stationary preparation ensemble is violated on IBM superconducting processors, so temporal drift produces context-dependent effective ensembles and a relaxed Bell bound |S| <= 2 + 6*delta_ens. Introduces an operational drift witness (delta_op) from bin-resolved outcome statistics for fixed measurement channels, which persists after readout mitigation.
papers.overlap_reason: Closest in spirit to the material's central narrative: drift on a superconducting device invalidates a conclusion drawn from repeated identical two-qubit entangled-state executions, and the drift survives readout mitigation. Their drift is resolved between runs within sessions rather than across sessions, they use CHSH rather than purity, and they do not compare the two timescales against each other.

papers.title: Decision Kernels for Quantum Error Mitigation: Why Accuracy Gains Need Not Improve Downstream Decisions
papers.authors: Vicenzo Scavino
papers.what_it_establishes: Quotient-space theory of finite-shot quantum error mitigation for downstream decisions, validated with Qiskit Aer simulations plus, per Section 12, 'a pre-registered hardware micro-cell stress test'. It reports a pre-specified criterion NOT being met and declines the corresponding claim: the hardware test supports the covariance prediction 'while its stricter decision-direction criterion is not met, so no device-level claim is made'. I read the full text for pre-registration language: the term appears essentially once, the specific device is not identified in what I could read, and no locking mechanism (registry, git commit, hash, timestamp) is described.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes that 'pre-registered' hardware stress tests with pre-specified criteria, including openly reporting a criterion that fails, already appear in 2026 quant-ph. But the pre-registration is thin (asserted, not documented), the hardware role is a small robustness probe rather than the study's spine, and there is no prediction-versus-measurement miss diagnosed to a vendor specification gap.

papers.title: Schedule-dependent basin occupation and instance-specific effective scales in cycled reverse annealing on programmable quantum annealers
papers.authors: Luis Lozano
papers.venue_year: arXiv preprint, quant-ph; v1 17 May 2026, v3 12 Aug 2026
papers.what_it_establishes: The closest published analogue. A commercial-quantum-hardware study (D-Wave Advantage2 and Advantage_system6.4) run under 'a locked analysis plan with a prior-knowledge disclosure', which reports openly that 'a pre-registered linear predictor of schedule sensitivity fails on held-out instances' (no model passed either held-out criterion; best r = -0.61, R^2 = -3.0), and that an earlier pilot's two-pause enhancement claim is contradicted (Fisher p=0.0013). The v3 comment records a substantive correction withdrawing v2's central claims after calibration, units, estimator and gauge-frame errors were found, with all analyses regenerated under the locked plan and raw QPU records unchanged. It also reports that the vendor solver 'did not expose a calibration epoch', so per-job calibration metadata was unavailable. VERIFIED AT FULL TEXT, and the full text contains the decisive distinction: the plan was locked AFTER a diagnostic reanalysis of the same archived data, and the author says so explicitly ('the plan was locked after a diagnostic reanalysis of the same archived data, so approximate values of several statistics it would recompute were already known'). Bias control therefore rested on calibrated permutation/bootstrap thresholds, mechanical decision rules, all-cells reporting with FDR control, and an archived prior-knowledge disclosure - not on prospective commitment.
papers.overlap_reason: Shares the core methodological move (locked plan on commercial quantum hardware, pre-registered predictor reported as failing, vendor calibration metadata unavailable, honest retraction) but differs on the one axis the material claims: this plan was locked retrospectively over archived data, not before measurement. Different platform class (annealer, not gate-model superconducting), different physics (basin occupation, not purity/shadow estimation), and no spec-versus-reality readout finding. This is the paper a referee will find first and the material must cite and distinguish on prospectivity.

papers.title: Modeling and mitigation of cross-talk effects in readout noise with applications to the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
papers.authors: Filip B. Maciejewski, Flavio Baccari, Zoltan Zimboras, Michal Oszmaniec
papers.what_it_establishes: Diagonal Detector Overlapping Tomography reconstructs k-local measurement cross-talk on N qubits using O(k 2^k log N) circuits built from random X/identity patterns -- i.e. the neighbours are set to random bit patterns, so multi-excitation configurations are sampled. Error reduction factors >22 (IBM 15q) and >5.5 (Rigetti Aspen 23q). Reports that correlations in the measurement noise do NOT follow the physical layout of the device.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes the correlated-readout-noise modelling framework and the random-multi-excitation calibration circuits, but reports no weight-dependence or saturation and no conditional P(1|0) figures. The 'correlations do not follow device layout' result is a caution for the material's neighbour-based framing.

papers.title: Mitigating measurement errors in multi-qubit experiments
papers.authors: Sergey Bravyi, Sarah Sheldon, Abhinav Kandala, David C. McKay, Jay M. Gambetta
papers.what_it_establishes: The continuous-time Markov process (CTMP) correlated readout model A = e^G, with a generator G built from single- and two-qubit error terms (2n^2 rates). Measured correlated two-qubit rates of a few percent for some pairs on a 12-qubit graph state and <1% for all pairs in a 20-qubit random Clifford experiment on ibmq_johannesburg; mean readout error (3.44 +/- 1.72)e-2; noise strength gamma ~ 0.05n. Tensor-product mitigation systematically over-estimates weight-3 to weight-6 stabilizers where CTMP agrees better.
papers.overlap_reason: This is the model the material's saturation claim should be argued AGAINST. A generator made of pairwise terms makes the effective error rate grow with the number of excited qubits (gamma ~ 0.05n), i.e. it predicts accumulation. An observed saturation is therefore a substantive contradiction of the field-standard correlated model, not merely a new datum -- worth framing that way explicitly.

papers.title: Mitigating Measurement Errors in Quantum Computers by Exploiting State-Dependent Bias
papers.authors: Swamit S. Tannu, Moinuddin K. Qureshi
papers.venue_year: MICRO-52: 52nd Annual IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Microarchitecture, 2019
papers.what_it_establishes: Establishes that readout error on superconducting devices is asymmetric -- |1> is substantially more error-prone than |0> because of relaxation during readout -- and exploits this by flipping qubits to measure in the stronger state. The associated line of work reports a strong correlation between readout error and the Hamming weight of the measured state on IBMQ machines.
papers.overlap_reason: Directly pre-empts the material's asymmetry finding ('asymmetric in the direction T1 decay during readout predicts') -- that is established, not new. It also stakes out Hamming-weight dependence of readout error as known, which narrows the material's saturation claim to the SHAPE of the weight curve rather than its existence. I verified the state-dependent-bias mechanism from the ACM record; I did NOT read the full text and could not verify the Hamming-weight figure inside this specific paper, so cite that sub-claim cautiously.

papers.title: Measurement Crosstalk Errors in Cloud-Based Quantum Computing
papers.authors: Seungchan Seo, Joonwoo Bae
papers.what_it_establishes: Uses quantum detector tomography to quantify measurement crosstalk on cloud services from IBM and Rigetti (IBMQ Yorktown and Rigetti Aspen-8), and identifies entanglement in the reconstructed three-qubit detector as a signature of crosstalk that single-qubit correction cannot remove.
papers.overlap_reason: Same 'characterise readout crosstalk on the cloud device you were actually given' posture as the material, on both vendors, four years earlier. I could not extract numeric magnitudes or any weight-dependence from the landing page, so the strength of the overlap on the material's specific numbers is unverified.

papers.title: Mitigation of correlated readout errors without randomized measurements
papers.authors: Adrian Skasberg Aasen, Andras Di Giovanni, Hannes Rotzinger, Alexey V. Ustinov, Martin Gaerttner
papers.what_it_establishes: Mitigation protocol using only single-qubit Pauli measurements and overlapping detector tomography, covering a broad class of correlated readout noise models and scaling to large registers; assessed in simulation up to 100 qubits using readout errors taken from superconducting-qubit experiments.
papers.overlap_reason: Current state of the art for correlated readout mitigation; establishes that correlated readout error is a live, actively modelled problem in 2025. No conditional-on-neighbour-excitation data and no weight dependence reported in what I could verify.

papers.title: Benchmarking the quality of multiplexed qubit readout beyond assignment fidelity
papers.authors: Andras Di Giovanni, Adrian Skasberg Aasen, Juergen Lisenfeld, Martin Gaerttner, Hannes Rotzinger, Alexey V. Ustinov
papers.what_it_establishes: Argues assignment fidelity is an inadequate single-number summary of multiplexed readout quality, uses detector tomography for full multiqubit readout characterisation, and proposes readout correlation coefficients and infidelity convergence as optimisation/validation tools.
papers.overlap_reason: Supports the material's broader thesis that a single published readout number is insufficient, and supplies correlation coefficients as an established metric. I could not verify from the abstract page whether they measure any dependence on the number of simultaneously excited qubits.

papers.title: Assessing the Stability of Noisy Quantum Computation
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Travis S. Humble
papers.venue_year: Proc. SPIE 12238, Quantum Communications and Quantum Imaging XX (2022); arXiv:2208.07219, 11 Aug 2022
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED WORK #2. This is the DEFINITIONAL paper, not a measurement paper. It separates four concepts that the field conflates: accuracy ('how close the experimentally realized output of a quantum program matches the known, correct output'), reproducibility ('how close an instance of a program is to a previously executed instance on the same or potentially different device'), reliability (deviation of device parameters such as gate fidelities from expectation), and stability ('quantifies whether the program behavior stays bounded in the presence of fluctuations due to noise'). Formalizes epsilon-accuracy as d_H <= epsilon and epsilon-reproducibility as Pr(d <= epsilon) >= 1 - delta. Derives operational bounds: for a single-qubit depolarizing channel, e <= 3*epsilon/4; an output-stability bound d_H <= sqrt(1 - sqrt(2*phi^2 - 1)); and a calibration-interval bound delta_t_stable under linear channel drift lambda(t) = lambda_0 - eta*delta_t. Empirical illustration is thin and deliberately so: a 4-qubit Bernstein-Vazirani circuit on ibmq_mumbai (27 qubits) compared between 17 June 2022 and 31 July 2022, plus initialization-fidelity maps on ibmq_washington (127 qubits) for Jan-Feb 2022 versus 31 May 2022, fitted with beta distributions. STATED LIMITATIONS: accuracy 'requires a priori knowledge of the noiseless reference distribution q, and this may be an impractical requirement'; and the framework's own premise, that 'the assumption that a NISQ noise channel is stationary does not hold up to experimental scrutiny. However, noise characterizations are assumed to be constant in current research when applying error mitigation.' Correlated readout error is not treated; register-size scaling is not examined beyond the one 4-qubit example.
papers.overlap_reason: This supplies the material's VOCABULARY, not its result. Everything the material reports is expressible in these terms: the SWAP-test miss is an accuracy failure with a KNOWN reference (purity 1), sidestepping the paper's own stated limitation about needing the noiseless distribution; the cross-session 0.2 purity swing is a reproducibility failure across instances on the same device; the missing readout spec is a reliability failure. What the material adds is the causal decomposition these authors leave open. They bound stability as a FUNCTION of device parameters assumed to be known and published; the material's finding is that the governing parameter was neither known nor published, and that supplying it (readout 0.89 -> 0.75, plus crosstalk -> 0.7163 against 0.7184 measured) closes a 17-standard-error gap to within one part in three hundred. That is an identification result, not a bound. Their depolarizing-channel assumption is also directly contradicted by the material's asymmetric, T1-directional, excitation-correlated readout channel.

papers.title: Modeling and mitigation of cross-talk effects in readout noise with applications to the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
papers.authors: Filip B. Maciejewski, Flavio Baccari, Zoltán Zimborás, Michał Oszmaniec
papers.what_it_establishes: A k-local correlated measurement-noise model characterized by Diagonal Detector Overlapping Tomography, with mitigation at the level of marginal distributions. Tested on a 15-qubit IBM device and a 23-qubit Rigetti device. Reports the structurally important negative result that correlations in measurement noise do NOT track the physical layout of the device. Mitigation improves errors by a factor >22 (IBM) and >5.5 (Rigetti). I could not verify from the abstract-level material whether state-conditional dependence or excitation-weight scaling is analyzed; the fetched summary indicates it is not, but I did not read the body.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes correlated readout noise as a modelled, mitigable phenomenon on BOTH IBM and Rigetti superconducting hardware, which pre-empts any framing of correlated readout as unrecognized. It does not, on the evidence I verified, resolve the dependence on the excitation weight of neighbours or report saturation, and its purpose is mitigation rather than the audit of a published specification. The material's contribution against it is the weight-resolved structure and the demonstrated propagation into a pre-registered physical estimate.

papers.title: Efficient reconstruction, benchmarking and validation of cross-talk models in readout noise in near-term quantum devices
papers.authors: Jan Tuziemski, Filip B. Maciejewski, Joanna Majsak, Oskar Słowik, Marcin Kotowski, Katarzyna Kowalczyk-Murynka, Piotr Podziemski, Michał Oszmaniec
papers.what_it_establishes: Efficient reconstruction of k-local cross-talk models in readout noise with logarithmic sample complexity, plus benchmarking and validation procedures. Applied to a 79-qubit Rigetti device and a 127-qubit IBM device, giving roughly 20% improvement in mitigation performance for correlated-clusters-and-neighbours models on MAX-2-SAT energy estimation. The abstract does not address weight dependence or saturation.
papers.overlap_reason: The most directly comparable readout-crosstalk characterization on RIGETTI hardware at scale, so it constrains any novelty claim about correlated readout on Rigetti specifically. Its target is scalable model reconstruction for mitigation; the material's target is the audit gap between the published specification and the measured device, and the weight law. I verified only the abstract, so I cannot rule out that a weight-resolved analysis appears in the body; this should be checked in full text before the material claims the weight structure is unprecedented.

papers.title: Measurement Crosstalk Errors in Cloud-Based Quantum Computing
papers.authors: Seungchan Seo, Joonwoo Bae
papers.what_it_establishes: Uses quantum detector tomography over cloud services to verify and characterize measurement readout errors on IBMQ and Rigetti platforms, documenting measurement crosstalk affecting multiple qubits simultaneously and noting entanglement as a crosstalk source in three-qubit measurements. Specific magnitudes and any state- or weight-dependence are not given in the abstract.
papers.overlap_reason: Same setting as the material, cloud-accessed superconducting hardware including Rigetti, same object, measurement crosstalk, and same posture of independent verification rather than trusting the platform. It is the closest precedent for 'we tomographed the detector ourselves rather than believing the cloud.' It does not compare against a published vendor specification, does not resolve excitation weight, and does not carry the result through to a pre-registered physical prediction.

papers.title: Impact of unreliable devices on stability of quantum computations
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Travis S. Humble
papers.venue_year: arXiv:2307.06833 (2023); ACM Transactions on Quantum Computing, doi:10.1145/3682071
papers.what_it_establishes: The most developed entry in the Dasgupta-Humble line and NOT currently cited by the material. Uses the 127-qubit ibmq_washington over January 2022 to April 2023 (16 months of daily noise measurements aggregated monthly), with a 5-qubit Bernstein-Vazirani benchmark and simulated 8- and 12-qubit variants. Derives an upper bound linking device reliability to outcome stability, s_max = 2c*sqrt(1 - (1 - H_normalized^2)^(2d)). Treats SPAM explicitly via Kraus operators for qubit-specific measurement fidelity and identifies SPAM AS THE LARGEST ERROR SOURCE. Notably, it uses Gaussian copulas specifically to preserve correlation information between noise parameters, since standard approaches fail to capture those dependencies in high dimensions. Finds fluctuation across minutes and days that 'significantly surpasses the maximum allowable threshold.' Limitations conceded: requires well-characterized device noise data as INPUT, a single device platform, and that 'achieving a 100% complete characterization of noise is difficult.'
papers.overlap_reason: Should be added to the material's bibliography; it is the strongest version of the cited authors' argument and it already reaches the conclusion that SPAM dominates, which anticipates part of the material's readout finding. But its stated dependency is the material's target: the method 'requires well-characterized device noise data as input,' and the material's result is that on this platform that input did not exist, was not published, and was wrong by 3x when measured. The material also supplies what this paper simulates rather than measures, namely register-size dependence at n=3 and n=4 on real hardware, and finds it non-monotonic in a way no noise-parameter bound of this form anticipates.

papers.title: Characterizing the Reproducibility of Noisy Quantum Circuits
papers.authors: Samudra Dasgupta, Travis S. Humble
papers.what_it_establishes: Bounds circuit reproducibility by device characterization metrics, measuring reproducibility as the Hellinger distance between computational results. Validated with single-qubit test circuits on a superconducting transmon processor with well-characterized readout and gate error rates, and with numerical simulation of Bernstein-Vazirani. Shows the minimum sample size for reproducibility is a nonlinear function of confidence level and accuracy threshold.
papers.overlap_reason: Completes the Dasgupta-Humble trilogy the material half-cites and should be added for scholarly completeness. Its premise, a processor 'with well-characterized readout and gate error rates,' is exactly the condition the material shows fails in the wild. The material's cross-session result is a measured counterexample to the implicit assumption that characterization transfers between sessions.

papers.title: Preparation nonstationarity in superconducting-qubit Bell tests (arXiv title: A Preparation Nonstationarity Loophole in Superconducting-Qubit Bell Tests)
papers.authors: Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, Ramakrishna Podila
papers.venue_year: Phys. Rev. A (2026), doi:10.1103/ydtx-yy5y; arXiv:2601.08290, 13 January 2026
papers.what_it_establishes: Shows that the standard assumption that repeated circuit executions sample a single stationary preparation ensemble is violated on contemporary superconducting hardware, with consequences for interpreting Bell violations. Introduces an ensemble-divergence framework in which slow temporal drift induces context-dependent effective ensembles even with measurement independence and locality preserved, yielding a relaxed Bell bound and a bin-resolved operational witness. Devices: ibm_fez (qubits 0,1) and ibm_torino (qubits 40,41). Timescale is SHORT: roughly 96 seconds of wall-clock per qubit pair across six temporal bins, with about 48 s separating readout-matrix calibrations. Observed drift delta_op approximately 0.06-0.09 (ibm_torino) and 0.062 (ibm_fez), p<0.05. Crucially, the drift PERSISTS AFTER full two-qubit readout mitigation, ruling out measurement artefacts. Scope is deliberately narrow: 'Our objective is not to survey or characterize this effect across all qubit pairs, but to establish its existence as a distinct mechanism.'
papers.overlap_reason: Strong methodological ally and a partial competitor on the drift axis, published seven months before the material's date. It establishes, on a two-qubit entangled-state observable, that drift is real and is NOT a readout artefact, which is a useful independent constraint on the material's own mechanism-elimination exercise. But its horizon is 96 seconds, entirely within a single session; it explicitly does not compare across sessions or days. The material's distinguishing measurement, cross-session drift on byte-identical circuits on the same physical qubits at roughly twenty times the within-session magnitude, lies wholly outside this paper's temporal reach, and the material's readout finding is the complement of theirs: they exclude readout as the cause of their effect, the material identifies readout as the cause of its prediction gap while a separate cross-session effect remains unexplained by it.

papers.title: Forensics of Error Rates of Quantum Hardware
papers.authors: Rupshali Roy, Swaroop Ghosh
papers.what_it_establishes: Motivated explicitly by the rise of third-party cloud providers offering quantum hardware as a service, where 'the actual execution of the program is not clearly visible to the customer' and published device information 'may not be accurate and/or correspond to the actual hardware allocated.' Infers relative backend error rates from the transpiler's own behaviour, ranking qubit links by transpiler selection frequency across many circuits, then compares those ranks against IBM's published ECR two-qubit error data. Predicts bin ranks within two levels for roughly 80-83.5% of qubit edges on the 127-qubit IBM Brisbane and Sherbrooke. Restricted to GATE errors: readout error is not treated.
papers.overlap_reason: The closest published articulation of the material's provenance problem: a user on a brokered platform cannot see or verify what actually ran, and the vendor's published numbers may not describe the allocated hardware. Any reviewer sceptical of the material's Bittensor-routed execution path should be pointed here, since it establishes that the concern is a recognized research problem rather than special pleading. It differs in remedy and in target: it infers GATE error ranks from transpiler telemetry on a conventional IBM cloud, whereas the material measures READOUT directly on a decentralized-broker path and finds the specification silent on that parameter. Complementary, not overlapping.

papers.title: Experimental shadow tomography beyond single-copy measurements
papers.authors: Xu-Jie Peng, Qing Liu, Lu Liu, Ting Zhang, You Zhou, He Lu
papers.what_it_establishes: Already known to the material (cited as peng2025beyond). Experimental implementation of shadow tomography using measurements beyond the single-copy setting, i.e. the experimental realization of the collective-measurement route the material's SWAP-test anchor also probes.
papers.overlap_reason: The existing experimental precedent for collective-measurement shadow protocols on hardware, so it bounds any claim of first experimental realization. It does not pre-register, does not audit vendor specifications, and does not report cross-session drift or a readout-traced prediction failure.

papers.title: Trustworthy Computing using Untrusted Cloud-Based Quantum Hardware
papers.authors: Suryansh Upadhyay, Swaroop Ghosh
papers.venue_year: arXiv preprint, 2 May 2023 (v1); 14 November 2024 (v2); related journal version in Frontiers in Computer Science 2024
papers.what_it_establishes: Models a future ecosystem in which untrusted, less-trusted, or unreliable vendors offer QPUs at varied price/performance points, and users are drawn to the cheaper and more available but less trusted hardware. Models adversarial tampering with results and proposes splitting shots across hardware options, plus a run-adaptive split heuristic exploiting temporal quality variation to identify untrustworthy hardware at runtime.
papers.overlap_reason: Anticipates the economic structure the material actually operated inside — a free/cheap tier routed through operators with unverified quality — and is the canonical citation for 'cheap tier implies weaker trust.' But its concern is deliberate result tampering, not specification incompleteness or drift, and it uses simulation of adversarial behaviour rather than a measured hardware campaign. It does not address whether a legitimate but opaque path degrades a scientific measurement.

papers.title: Measuring Control-Plane Openness in Near-Term Quantum Computing: A Rubric, Its Validation, and an Application to Thirteen Vendor Stacks
papers.authors: Rylan Malarchick
papers.what_it_establishes: Proposes a six-axis operational rubric for 'control-plane openness' — the layer between gate-level circuit specification and physical control electronics — defined so the same evidence yields the same grade across vendors. Applied to thirteen commercial vendors across superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom and photonic modalities as of 1 May 2026. Includes a reproducibility audit of pre-2025 IBM Qiskit Pulse experiments ported to Rigetti Quil-T as a demonstration of one of the harms detected.
papers.overlap_reason: The only work found that systematically GRADES vendors on what they expose to users, and it includes Rigetti and touches reproducibility harms from closed control planes. Useful as the citation for 'vendor disclosure varies and is measurable.' But it scores pulse-level and control-electronics access, not the contents of published performance specifications (whether readout error is listed), and not per-job calibration metadata or execution-path verifiability. I could not retrieve the per-vendor scores.

papers.title: Reproducible Builds for Quantum Computing
papers.authors: Iyán Méndez Veiga, Esther Hänggi
papers.what_it_establishes: Generalizes the reproducible-builds definition to the quantum setting under two threat models: confidentiality of user data during circuit preparation and submission, and INTEGRITY OF QUANTUM COMPUTATION RESULTS. Shows three examples of hiding classical information in transpiled circuits and two cases where minimal circuit modifications produce incorrect results.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes that the submission pipeline between user source and executed circuit is itself an attack surface and an integrity risk — relevant because the material's circuits traversed an extra mediation layer (aggregator plus distributed operators) before execution. Shows a circuit can be minimally altered en route with material effect on results. However it is a threat-model and toolchain paper with no hardware campaign, no drift analysis, and no engagement with vendor specification completeness.

papers.title: Rethinking Reproducibility in the Classical (HPC)-Quantum Era: Toward Workflow-Centered Science
papers.authors: Anna Vrtiak, Duuk Baten, Ariana Torres-Knoop
papers.what_it_establishes: Position paper arguing that scientific knowledge now depends on computational processes where hardware and software layers influence outcomes, and that quantum computing at low technological maturity amplifies existing reproducibility challenges while creating new ones through probabilistic outputs, hardware-specific noise, and tight software-hardware coupling. Proposes meta-workflows documenting both process abstractions and implementation contexts.
papers.overlap_reason: Conceptual framing only. Names 'infrastructure blends with the results,' which is a fair one-line description of the material's central problem, and is a reasonable citation for why quantum cloud results resist reproduction. It contains no measurement, no device access, and per my fetch does not discuss calibration metadata availability or device verification.
