papers.title: Microstructural Topology as a Prescriptor for Quantum Coherence: Towards A Unified Framework for Decoherence in Superconducting Qubits
papers.authors: Vinayak P. Dravid, Akshay A. Murthy, Peter Lim, Gabriel T. dos Santos, Ramandeep Mandia, James M. Rondinelli, Mark C. Hersam, Roberto dos Reis
papers.venue_year: arXiv preprint, quant-ph; v1 5 Apr 2026, v2 12 Apr 2026
papers.what_it_establishes: A separable framework for transmon decoherence in which 'Falsifiability is operationalized through a pre-committed 2x2 experimental protocol in which the variables must satisfy independent ratio checks within propagated uncertainty', plus a Minimum-Dataset Specification standardizing cross-laboratory reporting. Part I is conceptual and mathematical only; coordinated experimental validation is explicitly reserved for Part II.
papers.overlap_reason: Shows pre-commitment language entering mainstream superconducting-qubit physics from a well-known materials group, which is useful precedent for the material's framing. But no hardware was run, no prediction was measured, and no outcome is reported, so it cannot pre-empt a completed pre-registered measurement study.

papers.title: Validation of an Analysability Model in Hybrid Quantum Software
papers.authors: Ana Díaz-Muñoz, José A. Cruz-Lemus, Moisés Rodríguez, Mario Piattini, Maria Teresa Baldassarre
papers.what_it_establishes: An explicit 'registered report proposal' in a quantum context: a controlled experiment with human subjects across Italian and Spanish institutions to validate an analysability quality model for hybrid quantum-classical software.
papers.overlap_reason: The only registered report I found touching quantum computing at all, and it arrives via software engineering, where registered reports are an established format - not via physics. It concerns human comprehension of code, not quantum hardware measurement. Useful as evidence that the format reaches quantum research only through its computer-science border.

papers.title: Blind Analysis in Nuclear and Particle Physics
papers.authors: Joshua R. Klein, Aaron Roodman
papers.venue_year: Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science 55, 141-163 (2005)
papers.what_it_establishes: The canonical statement of physics's own answer to experimenter bias. Blind analysis prevents experimenters from knowing the answer until the analysis is complete; the review argues there is at least circumstantial evidence that bias has affected past measurements, and that as experiments grow costlier and harder to reproduce, the risk grows. Catalogues the practical blinding schemes in use.
papers.overlap_reason: Establishes the norms baseline the material must position against. Blinding and pre-registration are different instruments: blinding hides the answer so analysis choices cannot be tuned toward it; pre-registration fixes the claim so it cannot be revised after the answer is seen. The material does the latter. Physics has a strong institutional tradition of the former in particle, nuclear and dark-matter physics, and essentially none of either in quantum computing.

papers.title: Blind Analysis in Particle Physics
papers.authors: Aaron Roodman
papers.what_it_establishes: Reviews the blind-analysis technique, its historical development, the danger of experimenter bias, three distinct types of blind analysis, and BABAR's implementation.
papers.overlap_reason: Supporting norms citation alongside Klein and Roodman; documents that the discipline's bias-control vocabulary is 'blinding', not 'pre-registration'.

papers.title: Blind analysis in Physics experiments: Is this trip necessary?
papers.authors: Robert Golub
papers.what_it_establishes: An explicitly dissenting note: building on Klein and Roodman, it presents an alternate conclusion about the value of blind analysis in physics experiments. I verified the title, author, date and the one-sentence abstract; I did NOT read the full argument, so I can characterise the position only as skeptical.
papers.overlap_reason: Relevant because it shows the norms question is contested inside physics, not settled. A referee sympathetic to this view will ask the material to justify why pre-commitment was worth the cost; the material's answer (a >17 SE miss that would otherwise have been quietly re-derived) is a strong empirical reply and should be framed as one.

papers.title: Blinding multi-probe cosmological experiments
papers.authors: J. Muir, G. M. Bernstein, D. Huterer, et al. (Dark Energy Survey Collaboration)
papers.venue_year: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society; arXiv v1 13 Nov 2019, revised 4 May 2020
papers.what_it_establishes: Method for concealing inferred cosmological parameters until all analysis decisions are final, by shifting summary statistics while preserving internal-consistency checks; demonstrated on simulated DES clustering and lensing data. Motivated explicitly by preventing scientists from biasing analysis toward theoretically expected results, especially when new results are scrutinized for consistency with previous ones.
papers.overlap_reason: Second pillar of the physics norms baseline: cosmology institutionalized blinding, and did so precisely because results get judged against prior expectations. Establishes that when a physics subfield decides analyst bias is a live threat, it reaches for blinding rather than pre-registration - which is what makes the material's choice a methodological argument that needs making.

papers.title: A blinding solution for inference from astronomical data
papers.authors: Elena Sellentin
papers.venue_year: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (2020); arXiv 18 October 2019
papers.what_it_establishes: A joint blinding/deblinding strategy allowing up to three blinding stages - data, theory computation, and covariance matrix - applied to KiDS-450 weak lensing. Shows covariance blinding is especially effective, and that undetected covariance errors can bias conclusions in ways that mimic real tension.
papers.overlap_reason: Norms citation. Its substantive point is also thematically close to the material: an error in an unmodelled part of the uncertainty budget can masquerade as a physical discrepancy - the material's readout-specification gap is the hardware analogue.

papers.title: The preregistration revolution
papers.authors: Brian A. Nosek, Charles R. Ebersole, Alexander C. DeHaven, David T. Mellor
papers.venue_year: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA 115(11), 2600-2606 (2018)
papers.what_it_establishes: The standard reference defining pre-registration, its purpose (separating confirmatory from exploratory inference, blocking HARKing and undisclosed analytic flexibility), and the case for adoption across the sciences.
papers.overlap_reason: Definitional citation the material needs, since its audience will not know the term as a term of art. No quantum or physical-science content.

papers.title: The preregistration revolution needs to distinguish between predictions and analyses
papers.authors: Alison Ledgerwood
papers.venue_year: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA (2018), letter
papers.what_it_establishes: Argues that pre-registering a prediction and pre-registering an analysis plan are different acts with different epistemic force; Nosek et al. replied under the title 'Predictions without analysis plans are inert'.
papers.overlap_reason: Directly germane to how the material should describe itself. The material locked numeric point predictions (0.8932 purity, 1.500 anchor) to version control. Referees who know this literature will ask whether the analysis pipeline was locked too, or only the numbers. The material should state which, because this exchange is the standard place that question comes from.

papers.title: Preregistration for Experiments with AI Agents
papers.authors: Michelle Vaccaro
papers.what_it_establishes: A position paper cataloguing researcher degrees of freedom specific to a new computational experimental field and proposing a field-specific pre-registration template.
papers.overlap_reason: No quantum content. Included as the structural precedent for what a 'pre-registration for quantum hardware experiments' contribution looks like as a paper: enumerate the degrees of freedom the platform creates, then propose the template. If the material wants a methodological contribution rather than only a physics result, this is the model, and it shows the slot is filled in AI and empty in quantum.

papers.title: Wire-Level Interrupt-to-Decision Latency of On-Sensor MLC versus Host Inference on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano: A Pre-Registered Measurement Study
papers.authors: Swami, Sonawane (full given names not verified)
papers.what_it_establishes: A hardware measurement study carried out under an explicit pre-registration, with the pre-registration recorded as a README commit (commit 9c738a8, 2026-04-16) and a separate pilot-and-verdict commit two days later.
papers.overlap_reason: Not quantum, and not physics. Included for one specific reason: it is direct precedent for the exact mechanism the material uses - a git commit as the pre-registration timestamp for a hardware measurement study - so the material cannot claim that mechanism as novel, only its application to quantum hardware. Verified from search-result text quoting the commit hash and dates, not from the PDF itself.

papers.title: Scalable mitigation of measurement errors on quantum computers
papers.authors: Paul D. Nation, Hwajung Kang, Neereja Sundaresan, Jay M. Gambetta
papers.what_it_establishes: The M3 matrix-free mitigation method, working in the subspace of observed bitstrings and accommodating both uncorrelated and correlated errors; a correlated-M3 variant is reported to agree with the full assignment matrix, and Hamming-distance truncation is used to approximate the mitigation.
papers.overlap_reason: Standard tooling context, and its Hamming-distance truncation is the closest existing use of an excitation-weight-like structure in readout mitigation. It is a mitigation method, not a characterisation of the physical weight dependence, so it does not scoop the saturation claim.

papers.title: Crosstalk In Contemporary Quantum Devices
papers.authors: Spiro Gicev, Ben Harper, Haiyue Kang, Muhammad Usman, Martin Sevior
papers.what_it_establishes: A 2026 cross-platform review of crosstalk covering physical origins, mitigation and security implications. Its readout-crosstalk section notes that the state of adjacent qubits can affect a readout result in frequency-multiplexed superconducting systems, and focuses on machine-learning discrimination as the mitigation route.
papers.overlap_reason: Most valuable as NEGATIVE evidence for the novelty argument: the field's most recent survey, three months old, does not report saturation of readout crosstalk with excitation weight and does not raise vendor omission of readout error. Verified by fetching the HTML of v2 and asking directly about both points.

papers.title: Measurement-induced state transitions in multi-qubit transmon processors
papers.authors: Baptiste Hoyau, Alexander McDonald, Boris M. Varbanov, Manuel H. Munoz-Arias, Alexandre Blais
papers.what_it_establishes: Theory/characterisation of measurement-induced state transitions (MIST) when a transmon couples to other circuit elements. Reports that a spectator qubit can be affected by the measurement-induced transition of the qubit being read out, and conversely that the presence of a spectator LOWERS the MIST threshold of the read-out qubit.
papers.overlap_reason: Supplies a candidate physical mechanism for excitation-dependent readout error that is not simple resonator-tone leakage, and the reciprocal spectator effect is the kind of nonlinearity that could produce saturation. Relevant to the material's 'seven candidate mechanisms bounded or excluded' section; two transmons plus a coupler, not a device-scale study.

papers.title: Transmon qubit readout fidelity at the threshold for quantum error correction without a quantum-limited amplifier
papers.authors: Liangyu Chen, Hang-Xi Li, Yong Lu, Christopher W. Warren, Christian J. Krizan, Sandoko Kosen, Marcus Rommel, Shahnawaz Ahmed, Amr Osman, Janka Biznarova, Anita Fadavi Roudsari, Benjamin Lienhard, Marco Caputo, Kestutis Grigoras, Leif Groenberg, Joonas Govenius, Anton Frisk Kockum, Per Delsing, Jonas Bylander, Giovanna Tancredi
papers.what_it_establishes: Reports 99.5% two-state and 96.9% three-state assignment fidelity, and is the standard reference for readout physics in transmons -- relaxation during readout as the dominant error, and fidelity loss when readout drive amplitude excites higher levels.
papers.overlap_reason: Background for the material's asymmetry-in-the-T1-direction observation. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: search snippets circulating numbers of 97.3% (global ground state) versus 91.3% (global excited state) across 16 basis states could NOT be traced to this paper -- the abstract page does not contain them. Do not cite those figures to this reference without reading the full text.

papers.title: Tensor network characterization and mitigation of readout errors
papers.authors: Yuchen Guo, Shuo Yang
papers.what_it_establishes: Uses a matrix-product-operator model of the assignment map, reported in the listing metadata as capturing correlated readout errors that uncorrelated models miss.
papers.overlap_reason: Most recent correlated-readout characterisation work; included for completeness of the 2026 landscape. I only saw it through an arXiv API listing summary -- I did not read the abstract page or the paper, so nothing here should be cited without independent checking.

papers.title: Evaluating Calibration-Based Digital Twins for IBM Quantum Hardware Simulation
papers.authors: Edgars Bautra, Maksims Dimitrijevs, Abuzer Yakaryilmaz
papers.what_it_establishes: Builds noise models ('digital twins') from vendor-published calibration CSVs, including per-qubit readout assignment error, and compares them against real execution on ibm_brisbane and ibm_sherbrooke. Readout error enters only as independent per-qubit ReadoutError instances.
papers.overlap_reason: The nearest published instance of the material's 'prediction from published spec vs measured hardware' comparison. It does NOT decompose the residual gap by error source, does not identify readout as dominant, and does not consider correlated readout error -- so the material's reconciliation (0.89 -> 0.75 -> 0.7163 vs 0.7184 measured) is not pre-empted.

papers.title: Few-Shot Cross-Device Transfer for Quantum Noise Modeling on Real Hardware
papers.authors: Sahil Al Farib, Sheikh Redwanul Islam, Azizur Rahman Anik
papers.venue_year: arXiv:2604.24397, 27 April 2026; 9 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables; submitted to IEEE QCE 2026
papers.what_it_establishes: CITED WORK #3 (the 2026 few-shot paper). Trains a residual neural network to map noisy circuit output distributions to ideal ones on a source device and transfers it to a target device with few samples. Devices: ibm_fez (source) -> ibm_marrakesh (target). Dataset: 85 circuits per device, 170 paired samples total; 2-5 qubits, depth 2-8; four families (40 random, 15 Bell, 15 GHZ, 15 QFT); 8,192 shots per circuit. Results: zero-shot transfer KL divergence 1.6706; with 20 fine-tuning samples 1.1924, a 28.6% improvement, recovering 34.9% of the gap to in-domain performance. CX gate error is identified as the dominant cross-device mismatch, readout error second. CRITICALLY FOR OUR PURPOSES, its inputs and its stated limitations run the opposite way from the material: device features are pulled from IBM Quantum's CALIBRATION API at execution time rather than measured independently, features are mean-aggregated rather than per-qubit, and the authors state plainly that they 'do not control for temporal drift between backend executions' while noting that 'IBM Quantum calibration data drifts substantially over hours to days.' No predictions were pre-registered; the study is post-hoc. Five limitations are conceded: small dataset (170 samples, two devices), shallow circuits, mean-aggregated features, no drift modeling, and a simple architecture without classical baselines.
papers.overlap_reason: Same era, same platform family, opposite methodology and opposite conclusion structure. It treats vendor calibration as the trusted feature vector and learns a correction on top; the material treats vendor calibration as the untested hypothesis and finds it off by 3x in the one parameter the spec omits. It explicitly declines to control temporal drift, which is precisely the axis on which the material's largest effect lives (cross-session 0.2 in purity). It is a useful FOIL rather than a competitor: it demonstrates that the 2026 state of practice both depends on vendor readout numbers and knows it has not validated them. The material would add the missing validation, and would supply the drift control the paper lists as future work. There is no claim collision.

papers.title: Mitigating measurement errors in multi-qubit experiments
papers.authors: Sergey Bravyi, Sarah Sheldon, Abhinav Kandala, David C. McKay, Jay M. Gambetta
papers.what_it_establishes: Two measurement-error mitigation schemes by classical post-processing, based on a tensor-product noise model and on a correlated Continuous Time Markov Process (CTMP) model, with error rates extractable from calibration data by a simple formula. The CTMP model explicitly targets crosstalk arising from qubit-qubit coupling and spectral overlap of readout resonators. Demonstrated for measurements of up to 20 qubits.
papers.overlap_reason: The canonical correlated-readout mitigation reference and the standard baseline any reviewer will expect. It establishes that correlated readout is modelled and correctable in principle, which means the material should not claim novelty for the existence of correlated readout. It is a mitigation method paper on IBM hardware, not a measurement of how the correlation scales with the number of excited neighbours, and not an audit of vendor disclosure.

papers.title: Detecting and tracking drift in quantum information processors
papers.authors: Timothy Proctor, Melissa Revelle, Erik Nielsen, et al.
papers.what_it_establishes: A fast, statistically sound spectral-analysis technique for resolving time dependence in quantum processor data, applicable to time-series from any quantum processor experiment. Demonstrates that the widely used characterization tools assume static error modes and rates, which causes unheralded failures, misidentified error modes and wasted experimental effort. Validated on simulations and trapped-ion experiments, and shown to resolve time dependence within randomized benchmarking, gate set tomography and Ramsey spectroscopy.
papers.overlap_reason: The foundational reference establishing that quantum-processor errors are non-stationary and that standard characterization silently assumes otherwise, so it forecloses any claim that instability itself is a new observation. It is a methods paper on detecting drift in time-series, mostly on trapped ions, and it says nothing about vendor specification completeness, readout crosstalk versus excitation weight, or register-size non-monotonicity. Cite as background, not as competition.

papers.title: Computational references are not experiments: pre-registered validation of machine-learned sodium-cathode voltages
papers.authors: Krishna Teja Vepa
papers.what_it_establishes: Not a quantum paper, included as the clearest methodological precedent for the material's protocol. Commits verdict thresholds, failure modes and primary metrics to version control BEFORE analysis, then tests machine-learned cathode voltages against experimental literature values (n=6 after documented exclusion). Finds MAE 0.67 V, a conservative 95% bound of 1.09 V, strongly voltage-dependent residuals (r = -0.94), and that the computational reference database itself carries roughly 0.54 V of systematic error, dominating accuracy more than the model does. Outcome: the screening approach was retired and a follow-up calibration audit pre-registered.
papers.overlap_reason: Structurally the same argument in a different science: predictions frozen in version control before the data existed, a documented miss, and the miss traced to a systematic error in the REFERENCE rather than in the model. That is precisely the shape of the material's finding, where the wrong input is the parameter the specification does not publish. Useful as a citation for the pre-registration protocol and for the 'the reference is the problem' framing. Zero subject-matter overlap; it cannot contest any physics claim.

papers.title: JigSaw: Boosting Fidelity of NISQ Programs via Measurement Subsetting
papers.authors: Poulami Das, Swamit Tannu, Moinuddin Qureshi
papers.what_it_establishes: Shows that measuring a SUBSET of qubits yields lower measurement error than measuring all qubits, because it reduces measurement crosstalk, and exploits the more accurate local distributions to improve the full-register result. Related reported evidence in this line: measurement error rates rise by up to 2% when five qubits are measured simultaneously versus a single qubit in isolation.
papers.overlap_reason: Bears directly on the material's non-monotonicity finding as a COMPETING MECHANISM that must be addressed, and it happens to push the opposite way: measurement crosstalk grows with the number of qubits measured, so it predicts the smaller n=3 register should do BETTER, not worse. That makes it evidence FOR the material's claim that the observed ordering flip (n=3 worse than n=4 despite the n=4 register containing the n=3 one) is not explained by measurement crosstalk. It should be cited in the mechanism-elimination section rather than as prior art on the phenomenon.

papers.title: Isolating Recurring Execution-Dependent Abnormal Patterns on NISQ Quantum Devices
papers.authors: Zhenyu Qi et al. (full author list not verified)
papers.what_it_establishes: A delta-debugging framework showing that 'semantically equivalent circuits with identical compiler-visible costs can still produce unexpected hardware noise.' Identifies 25 recurring abnormal gate patterns, short ordered gate sequences on specific qubit neighbourhoods that induce excess error beyond current noise models. Three IBM Heron r2 backends across 30 qubit layouts (ibm_fez, ibm_marrakesh named), validated ACROSS CALIBRATION WINDOWS so that patterns are recurring rather than one-off. Compares real-device error against calibration-based error from the standard noise model, focusing on the discrepancy. Reports 24% and 45% noise reduction on the two backends.
papers.overlap_reason: Same core move as the material at the methodological level: take the discrepancy between the calibration-based model prediction and the real device as the object of study, and show the standard noise model omits something structural. Its omission is gate-sequence-and-layout dependent excess error on IBM Heron; the material's is readout magnitude, excitation-weight-dependent readout correlation, and cross-session non-stationarity on Rigetti via a broker. Its cross-calibration-window validation is a good precedent for the material's cross-session protocol.

papers.title: Verified delegated quantum computation requires techniques beyond cut-and-choose
papers.authors: Not verified — I did not retrieve the author list
papers.what_it_establishes: Concerns delegated quantum computation, in which a client with limited quantum capability outsources computation to an untrusted quantum server while preserving correctness and privacy, and argues that verification requires techniques beyond cut-and-choose. Represents the cryptographic verification tradition (blind and verifiable delegated quantum computing).
papers.overlap_reason: Included to close the lens rather than because it competes. The cryptographic verification literature (this, plus verifiable blind quantum computing generally) proves what a client CAN certify about an untrusted server in principle, under protocol assumptions the material's setup does not satisfy — the material submitted plain OpenQASM through a commercial aggregator with no verification protocol. Different problem, different assumptions, no result in contention. Worth one sentence in Related Work only to say why this tradition does not apply.

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Purity Amplification
papers.authors: Zhaoyi Li, Honghao Fu, Takuya Isogawa, Caio Silva, Isaac Chuang
papers.what_it_establishes: Per the arXiv API listing: an optimal quantum purity amplification protocol with experimental validation on superconducting quantum processors, aimed at NISQ noise.
papers.overlap_reason: Concerns increasing the purity of a state (a mitigation/distillation primitive), not estimating purity and not comparing measurement strategies. Included only to record that it surfaced in the purity-on-superconducting-hardware sweep and was ruled out. arXiv API listing only; abstract not fetched.

papers.title: Rigetti Announces General Availability of 108-Qubit System (Cepheus-1-108Q specification)
papers.authors: Rigetti Computing, Inc. (corporate press release, filed with the SEC and mirrored by Quantum Computing Report)
papers.what_it_establishes: NOT prior art but the load-bearing source for the material's central claim, and I verified it independently. The published specification gives: 108 qubits as twelve interconnected 9-qubit chiplets; 99.1% median two-qubit gate fidelity; 99.9% median single-qubit fidelity; ~60 ns gate speed; a 99.9%-at-28-ns CZ prototype benchmark; a stated target of 99.5% median two-qubit fidelity later in 2026; availability via Rigetti QCS and Amazon Braket. NO READOUT OR MEASUREMENT FIDELITY FIGURE APPEARS ANYWHERE. The only readout-adjacent statement is qualitative: upgraded control electronics 'intended to provide a higher signal-to-noise ratio for qubit readout,' with no number attached. I confirmed this omission on the Quantum Computing Report page listing every quoted specification; the investor-relations page itself timed out on fetch, so the confirmation rests on the mirror plus the search-result summaries of the release, which agree on every figure.
papers.overlap_reason: Source document rather than competing work. Recorded here because the material's thesis, that 'the input that was wrong is exactly the one the specification does not publish,' depends on this omission being real, and it is: the published Cepheus-1-108Q specification quantifies one- and two-qubit gate fidelity and gate speed and is silent on readout. This also resolves a separate provenance issue for the authors, since these device specifications trace to the Rigetti press release and not to the Open Quantum whitepaper.
